purpose: Reframe hooks bootstrap from PREVENTION-oriented (block stale tooling) to ENCOURAGEMENT-oriented (guide toward correct tools). Per user directive 2026-05-18: 'rather than preventing stale reference, it may be more productive to encourage the correct tools'. Less police, more guide.

design_philosophy_shift.before: Hooks BLOCK incorrect tool invocations (PreToolUse rejects grit/rtk/icm calls; PostToolUse fails build on stale spec versions)
design_philosophy_shift.after: Hooks GUIDE toward correct tools (SessionStart injects canonical primitives; PostToolUse suggests improvements when stale pattern detected; templates pre-populate correct values)
design_philosophy_shift.rationale: Prevention creates friction + adversarial UX (agent fights hook). Encouragement creates positive-reinforcement loop (agent learns the correct pattern by exposure + suggestion). User pushback against preventive design — sound /idea-refine pushback.

Direction_A_was_PREVENTION_now_ENCOURAGE.new_pattern: PreToolUse(Bash) detects grit/rtk/icm intent; suggests `oya vcs <equivalent-subcommand>` template; does NOT block (agent autonomously chooses; receives correct-tool guidance)

hooks_reframed.behavior: On detecting grit/rtk/icm/vox in Bash command, prints suggestion 'Consider: oya vcs <subcommand>'; does NOT exit non-zero; agent decides
On Agent dispatch, prints canonical-template suggestions (audience declaration; catalog check; version sources); does NOT block; informs
On new µservice creation outside current PR vertical, prints scope note + suggests current vertical's appropriate target; does NOT block

Direction_B_VERIFICATION_unchanged.rationale: Verification hooks (cargo build / line counts / orphan detection / artifact count bar) are MEASUREMENT, not enforcement. They report; they don't block. Keep as designed.
Direction_B_VERIFICATION_unchanged.behavior_clarified: PostToolUse hooks emit advisory output to stdout (becomes Claude's context per Claude Code session hooks); never exit non-zero on quality regressions; let agent decide whether to fix or queue

Direction_C_ORIENTATION_becomes_PRIMARY.elevation: Direction C (lifecycle orientation hooks) was 'highest single-hook leverage'; in the encouragement reframe, it BECOMES the dominant pattern

primary_hooks.behavior: Inject CLAUDE.md + latest handoff doc + canonical primitives list (oya vcs, OpenAPI 3.2.0, AsyncAPI 3.1.0, foundry-internal/intelligence-consumer, etc.) into session context
On UserPromptSubmit, append 'canonical primitive cheatsheet' to session (read-only; no blocking)
On Stop, check dirty cargo + new ADR-NNNN refs without files + lane regressions; suggest 'consider running X before close'

example_1_grit_to_oya_vcs.user_input: Agent runs `grit done --agent close-out` in Bash
example_1_grit_to_oya_vcs.old_behavior_prevention: Hook BLOCKS execution; exit 1 with error 'grit is retired'
example_1_grit_to_oya_vcs.new_behavior_encouragement: Hook prints to stderr: 'ℹ Note: grit is retired per ADR-0116. Canonical VCS primitive is `oya vcs` via `cargo run -p oya-dev-cli -- vcs <subcommand>`. Agent: consider rewriting your command and continue.' Exit 0; agent autonomously decides to rewrite.

example_2_session_start_orientation.new_behavior: Hook injects into Claude's context: 'CANONICAL PRIMITIVES for this project (2026-05-18): VCS = oya vcs (not grit). Contracts = OpenAPI 3.2.0 + AsyncAPI 3.1.0 + proto3 (not 3.3 / 3.0.0). AI = microservices/intelligence/ (consumer) + microservices/intelligence/ (internal Hermes). Plugin/app store ≠ marketplace ≠ community. Multi-context platform per ADR-0215. Vertical-slice rollout per ADR-0217. Buildability bar: 100+ artifacts per µservice. No-code-first UX with optional AI-assist.' This is read-only context; agent sees it but is not blocked by it.

example_3_spec_version_guide.old_behavior_prevention: PostToolUse hook fails; agent must fix to proceed
example_3_spec_version_guide.new_behavior_encouragement: PostToolUse hook prints suggestion: 'ℹ Detected OpenAPI version 3.3.0. As of 2026-05-18, latest OpenAPI is 3.2.0 (per spec.openapis.org). Consider correcting unless you have a verified source for 3.3.0.' Exit 0; agent decides.

hooks_to_drop_from_original_design: Strict blocking semantics in pre-dispatch-validate.sh (replaced by guide variant)
implementation_implications_for_pr_158: All hooks emit advisory output to stderr/stdout; never exit non-zero on quality concerns
Hooks that PROVIDE TEMPLATES (e.g., 'here's the oya vcs equivalent') are higher-value than hooks that BLOCK
Session-start orientation becomes the primary leverage point — invest most in this hook
Hooks are AGENT-FACING DOCUMENTATION delivered at the right moment, not policy enforcement
Reduces friction; agent retains autonomy; correct patterns spread by exposure
user_directive_pushback_acknowledged: User pushed back against my prevention-oriented design with /idea-refine pattern. The encouragement-oriented reframe is BETTER design: less adversarial, more like a senior engineer pair-programming with the junior agent. ADR-0221 (Agentic Development Pipeline Hardening) should explicitly call out this shift: hooks are GUIDANCE infrastructure, not enforcement infrastructure. CI gates (registry/quality/lanes.yaml) are the enforcement layer — they're shipped IN code review for human discussion, not at run-time blocking AI autonomy.
